```{r "intro"}
#| echo: false
intro <- tryCatch(
    {
        description <- packageDescription("GenE2scRNAseqIntro")
        pkg <- description$Package
        version <- description$Version
        authors <- eval(parse(text = description$Authors))
        license <- description$License
        glue::glue(
            "**Package:** {pkg}<br/>\n",
            "**Authors:** {paste(format(authors, include = c('given', 'family', 'role')), collapse = ', ')}<br/>\n",
            "**Compiled:** {as.character(Sys.Date())}<br/>\n",
            "**Package version:** {version}<br/>\n",
            "**R version:** <b style='color:red;'>{R.version.string}</b><br/>\n",
            "**BioC version:** <b style='color:red;'>{BiocManager::version()}</b><br/>\n",
            "**License:** {license}<br/>"
        )
    },
    error = function(e) {"Local preview"}
)
```

`r intro`

# Welcome {-}

This book supports a **2h30 live-coding workshop** on the analysis of
single-cell RNA-seq data with [Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org), taught
in the *Single-Cell Omics and Spatial Transcriptomics* teaching unit of the
GenE2 Master 2.

Starting from the UMI count matrix of an adult human testis, you will learn to:

- explain how a droplet-based experiment turns cells into a matrix of UMI
  counts;
- store and explore single-cell data in a `SingleCellExperiment`;
- run the standard pre-processing workflow: quality control, normalisation,
  feature selection, dimensionality reduction and batch correction;
- cluster cells, find the genes that mark each cluster, and name the clusters,
  by hand and against a public reference;
- test for differential expression with pseudobulk samples, the unit of
  replication being the donor, not the cell.

## How this book is organised {-}

| Chapter | Content | When |
|---|---|---|
| @sec-10x | How a 10x Genomics experiment produces a count matrix | read **before** the session (~15 min) |
| @sec-workshop | The hands-on session, all on one page | **live**, 2h30 |

## What you need to know {-}

Basic R: vectors, data frames, indexing with `[`, calling functions and loading
packages with `library()`. No prior experience of Bioconductor is needed: the
workshop introduces the containers it uses as it goes.

# The workshop environment {-}

Everything the workshop needs comes in a single `Docker` image, built from this
repository by GitHub Actions: R, Bioconductor and every package of the book,
plus the count matrix and the reference data, downloaded in advance.

👉 [ghcr.io/js2264/gene2scrnaseqintro](https://github.com/js2264/GenE2-scRNAseq-intro/pkgs/container/gene2scrnaseqintro) 🐳

## During the session: Orchestra {-}

Each participant gets their own RStudio Server, running from the workshop image
on the [Orchestra platform](https://orchestraplatform.org): nothing to install.

1. Follow the link shared by the instructor, and launch the workshop: an
   RStudio session opens in your browser (starting it can take a minute).
2. Create a new R script (*File* > *New File* > *R Script*) and save it: this
   is where you will type the code of the session.
3. A copy of the workshop page, `workshop/workshop.qmd`, is in your home
   directory, in case you lose track of the shared screen.

::: {.callout-warning icon='true'}

## Your instance is temporary

Workshop instances do not last forever: download your script and anything else
you want to keep (*Files* pane > *More* > *Export*) before the end of the day.

:::

## After the session: Docker {-}

The same environment runs on any computer with Docker installed. Start an
RStudio Server from the image:

```{sh "rstudio", filename="bash"}
#| eval: false
docker run \
    --volume <local_folder>:<destination_folder> \
    -e PASSWORD=gene2 \
    -p 8787:8787 \
    ghcr.io/js2264/gene2scrnaseqintro:devel
```

then open [http://localhost:8787](http://localhost:8787) and log in as
`rstudio`, with the password set above (`gene2`). For an R console only:

```{sh "docker", filename="bash"}
#| eval: false
docker run -it ghcr.io/js2264/gene2scrnaseqintro:devel R
```

## On your own computer {-}

You need R (>= 4.6.0), a recent Bioconductor and about 8 GB of RAM. The
workshop's R package lists every package used in the book, so installing it
with its dependencies installs them all:

```{r "install"}
#| eval: false
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("js2264/GenE2-scRNAseq-intro", dependencies = TRUE)
```

The count matrix is downloaded from GEO the first time you run the workshop
code, and cached for later sessions.

# The dataset {-}

The hands-on session analyses the adult human testis atlas of @guo2018: 6,490
cells from three healthy young donors, captured in two technical replicates
each with the 10x Genomics Chromium platform
([GSE112013](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE112013)).
@sec-dataset explains why it makes a good teaching dataset.
